paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1/2 use pastel worker/order/module colors with black or blue flow; Figures 3/4/6 use a stable categorical method palette (Triple-BERT blue, ablations orange/green, baselines red/purple/brown/pink/gray); Figure 5 reuses pastel module colors. Tables remain grayscale with bold best cells and occasional × failure marks.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The six figures are embedded raster image objects with vector captions and surrounding text; PDF page 3/4 image objects are exact public PNG assets, while later plots/diagrams have no public source. Tables, captions, rules, and body text are vector PDF objects. Figure 6 uses separate raster panels on pages 28 and 29.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L/Computer Modern math is consistent in body, captions, and tables; figure labels use small sans-serif text. Single-column Letter layout, booktabs-like rules, method ordering, and metric columns remain stable, but Figure 6 and the six-panel figures are color- and density-heavy at print size.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Workflow: At each time step, the worker and order pools update their states based on the assignments made in the previous time step. Specifically, the order pool adds newly arrived orders and removes overdue ones. For IDDQN, the Q-value of each worker-order pair is calculated, and ILP is applied to maximize the global Q-value. For TD3, the probability of each worker-order pair is computed, followed by the application of ILP to maximize the global assignment probability.

color.semantic_mapping: Worker/order pools, training stage, score/probability matrices, and flow direction use pastel fills, black/blue arrows, and textual module labels.

encodings.color: Worker versus order tokens and IDDQN/TD3/Q-value/probability modules.
encodings.shape: Rounded token/module rectangles and bipartite edges.
encodings.line: Solid arrows for information flow; dashed boxes for stages/pools.
encodings.facet: Worker Pool/Order Pool, IDDQN/TD3 central paths, Assignment output.
encodings.text: Update State, pool labels, ILP/BiPartite Matching, Add/Delete order callouts.

figures.data_and_statistics: Workflow-only raster diagram; no measured sample, aggregate, replication, or uncertainty. The example worker/order indices and pair nodes show a variable pool and matching operation, not observations.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 2 formalizes S,A,R,P after the workflow; Section 3.1 connects it to action decomposition and two-stage IDDQN→centralized TD3, while Appendix B/D supplies matching constraints and algorithms. Table 1 repeats the algorithm and reward-scope transitions.
design_strengths: Closes dynamic pool updates, two policy paths, ILP, and assignment in one loop.
Bipartite matching makes the large action-space solution concrete.
The exact public PNG can be compared byte/pixel-wise with the PDF image object.
design_weaknesses: Dense arrows and small pair grids make local flow hard to follow.
Training-stage and deployment-stage semantics are shown together without a legend.
Reward weights, unavailable-worker constraints, and solver cost are not encoded.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a single state-pool loop with parallel policy branches and a final global matching block; attach object-arrival/deletion operations to the loop entry.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Network Architecture: The network consists of three main components: the feature extractor, the actor sub-network, and the critic sub-network. First, a worker encoder and an order encoder are used to extract features from individual worker and order information, respectively. Then an Actor BERT model captures the relationships between them and a QK-Attention module calculates the selection probabilities for each worker-order pair. Finally, the fused features of the selected worker-order pairs are input into two separate Critic BERT models for further information extraction, and two Critic MLPs compute the Q-values, as TD3 requires two critics. (In this figure, the fused sequence (input to Critic-BERT) represents workers 1, 3, 6, and n selecting orders 2, 3, 4, and m, respectively.)

figures.data_and_statistics: Architecture-only raster diagram; the fused sequence example is workers 1,3,6,n selecting orders 2,3,4,m. No axes, sample count, metric aggregation, uncertainty, or runtime measurement is encoded.

Figure 1 supplies the system-level flow; Figure 3/Table 10 provide training and encoder evidence. The public img/AC-BERT.png equals the embedded PDF image pixel-for-pixel.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Training Process: Each method is trained five times, and the curve is smoothed using Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with α = 0.1. The shaded area represents the standard deviation.

figures.data_and_statistics: Five training runs per method; curves are sampled every 10 episodes and smoothed by EMA α=0.1. Shaded bands are standard deviation. Reward and service are higher-is-better; delivery/detour/pickup/confirmation require metric definitions and trade-off reading. No raw curve table or seed list is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4 first uses Figure 3 for training dynamics and the two main removals (without Stage 1 and without positive QK normalization); Table 4 gives weighted averages, Figure 4 tests policy-noise choices, and Figure 6 expands by order amount.
design_strengths: Shared axes and six metric panels show learning and cost together.
Five-run SD bands make convergence variability visible.
The legend includes both proposed variants and established baselines.
design_weaknesses: Eight color series and one in-panel legend are crowded.
Different metric directions mean vertical height is not uniformly better.
No direct curve values, seed identities, or uncertainty beyond the band definition.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a shared-scale small-multiple grid for reward, service, and operational costs, with identical run aggregation and an explicit band definition.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 establishes the dynamic pool→policy→ILP workflow; Figure 2 expands Worker/Order Encoder, Actor/Critic BERT, QK-Attention and ARL; Figure 3 gives training trajectories and two main removals; Tables 1–2 provide baseline and distribution-shift results; Appendix Figure 4/5 and Tables 3–10 expand noise, Stage 1, configurations, periods, scaling, Queens, positional embedding, and encoder conditions; Figure 6 provides order-volume detail.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 1/2 captions explain data flow, Figure 3/4 define EMA and bands, and Figure 5/6 are title-only. Table 1/4 define bold, Table 2/8 identify datasets, and Table 7 defines units, but most captions omit ±, ×, completed-only denominators, hardware, or weighting details that appear in prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use a stable Method/Encoder/Scenario identity column followed by reward, service, time, configuration, or resource columns. Multi-level/diagonal headers appear for Table 7 driver×order and Table 9 PE×order amount; other tables use one-level metric headers and horizontal row-group rules.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 1–2 define centralized SARL, action decomposition, ILP, BERT/QK and critic interfaces; Figure 3/Table 4 test Stage 1 and normalization removals; Figure 4 tests noise; Table 9 tests positional embedding; Table 10 tests ARL versus MLP; Tables 1/2/5/6/8 and Figure 6 supply baseline, shift, scale, and scenario outcomes.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figure 1/2 and Figure 3 plus Tables 1/2 carry the workflow, architecture, training dynamics, main baseline, and FHV shift. Appendix Figure 4/5 and Tables 3–10 provide implementation settings, noise, Stage 1, weighted periods, date/driver/order scaling, Queens, PE failure, and encoder heterogeneity; Figure 6 spans p.28–29 as a single detailed result.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Body/caption/table typography is PDF-confirmed Nimbus Roman No9 L with Computer Modern math; raster figures use estimated sans-serif labels around 6–10 pt and larger module titles. The caption/table serif system is stable, while dense raster panels lose readability at small size.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Method colors recur across Figures 3/4/6, and worker/order pastel roles recur across Figures 1/2/5. The palette is not source-parameter-locked for later raster figures; table objects remain grayscale and use text/bold/× rather than color.

most_reusable_patterns: Use a workflow loop to connect dynamic entity pools, parallel policy stages, a global matching solver, and the next state.
Pair an architecture overview with module insets for encoder/actor/critic/QK/ARL details.
Use fixed-order 2×3 metric small multiples with explicit run count, EMA, and dispersion semantics.
Keep model regime, capacity, resource cost, reward, service, and time costs in one table, and expose scaling/failure conditions in structurally identical appendix tables.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: end-to-end dynamic dispatch and ILP workflow with an exact public asset.
Figure 2: highest-information network interface showing BERT/QK/ARL/twin critics.
Figure 3 plus Table 4: training dynamics, uncertainty, and Stage 1/normalization failures.
Table 2 plus Figure 6: distribution and order-volume trade-offs with dispersion.
Tables 7/9/10: runtime, positional-embedding failure boundary, and encoder heterogeneity.
failure_patterns: Eight-color raster figures and small in-panel legends have weak grayscale/small-size readability.
Most appendix reward tables are point estimates without seeds or dispersion; scale/generalization claims are reward-only.
Table 1 changes centralization, algorithm, reward scope, backbone, and capacity together, so it is not a component-isolation comparison.
Figure 5 and Table 7 do not provide direct Stage 1/solver complexity measurements; Table 9 does not define the × failure state.
Completed-only delivery/detour values, higher confirmation time, and Queens pickup penalties are stated in prose but not always in captions.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: 用全局 worker/order→BERT/QK→ILP 流程建立 centralized SARL 接口，用 Figure 3 和主表展示 reward–service–time trade-off，再以附录的噪声、规模、分布转移、长度失败和 encoder 表格约束适用边界。
